newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary coalition agrees minister's replacements.
newsitem.headline: Hungary coalition agrees minister's replacements.

text.p: Hungary's government said on Thursday two parties of the ruling coalition agreed about the appointees to replace Tamas Suchman, sacked as industry and trade minister and minister responsible for privatisation.
"There was no debate on the nomination of Szabolcs Fazakas as industry and trade minister," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the government session.
The junior party of the coalition, the SZDSZ, also acknowledged that Fazakas would not supervise privatisation, and accepted a proposal to nominate Judit Csiha as privatisation minister, Kiss added.
Suchman and the state privatisation agency APB's board of directors were sacked in a scandal over irregular payments from the state privatisation agency APV to an advisor.
Kiss said Fazakas would be appointed following a hearing in a committee of parliament next week, adding the government would set up APV's new director board next Thursday.
Fazakas was state secretary at the industry and trade ministry until the summer, when he was named ambassador to Germany, Hungary's biggest trade partner.
Csiha is a lawyer who is state secretary at the justice ministry.
